insights.summary: FY26 revenue rose to ₹4,745 Cr with reported EBITDA of ₹628 Cr (13.2%), and PAT turned positive; Q4 revenue grew 37% with a 15.1% margin. Order inflows more than doubled to ₹7,687 Cr, largely North American data-centre projects and Indian telecom contracts, taking the open order book to ₹7,309 Cr. Management kept its target of a 20% reported EBITDA margin by the end of FY27 and expects enterprise and data centres to reach 30% of revenue this year.

what_changed.text: 20% reported EBITDA margin by the end of FY27
Enterprise and data centre to be 30% of revenue in FY27 (earlier 12-18 months away)
About ₹500 Cr capex for data-centre products and technology
Net debt to EBITDA ambition cut to below 1.2x

tone.label: confident
tone.quote:
This is not a cyclical uptick. It is a durable high visibility
growth opportunity playing out right here in our home market in India.

analyst_questions.answer: Germanium and helium remain costly and scarce; availability expected to improve quarter by quarter.
Supplying data centres already; working on long-term contracts, no names or sizes.
STL avoids the spot market and sells on long-term contracts.
Appeal filed in September 2025; two more appeal stages possible on the ~$100 million liability.

red_flags.text: About $100 million Prysmian judgment under appeal.
Germanium and helium shortages limit output; polymer costs up with the West Asia war.
Connectivity attach rate fell to 15% from 22%.
No revenue guidance and no capacity or utilisation disclosure.

watch_next: EBITDA margin moving towards 20% through FY27

business_snapshot.what_they_make: Optical fibre, fibre-optic cables (including high-fibre-count IBR cables), connectivity products and pre-terminated data-centre solutions (Neuralis); STL Digital IT services
business_snapshot.customers: Telecom operators, data centres and hyperscalers, citizen networks (BharatNet, BEAD) in North America, Europe and India
business_snapshot.revenue_mix: FY26: North America 39%, Europe 40%; enterprise and data centre 19%
business_snapshot.demand_drivers: AI data centres, FTTH roll-outs, 5G densification, government rural broadband
